- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates upside; add 1–3% to forecast for momentum-driven moves.
- Model tends to lag in early days of new sentiment shifts; if sentiment changes direction within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price reaction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast and avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates mean reversion; if price deviates >3σ from 30-day mean, adjust forecast toward mean by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misread sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in bullish signals.
